title: Tutorials: the Components track
goal:
The walkthrough the user asked for by name: make something once, reuse it, and change copies safely without breaking the link to the original.

The guides in this track: Make a component; Use it again and again; Override one copy; One name, two looks. The last one was planned as "Variants" and is named for what the app actually calls it, which is Versions.
notes:
One of the seven track tasks. Depends on the framework task and on the Help menu IA task.

What this track is for: The user named this one specifically: "maybe a building components walkthrough". Source of truth is docs/design/ui-building.md plus ComponentInstances and ComponentVersionMatching in PhotonzCore. The hard idea to teach is what a copy owns and what it does not - an override sticks, everything else is refilled from the original on the next sync - and the recent work on a copy wearing its own text style is a good concrete example to build the override guide on.

Write the guides as DATA in the catalogue. If a guide in this track cannot be expressed without new framework machinery, that is a finding: file it against the framework rather than special casing it here, and say so in the audit.

---
SHARED CONTEXT for every tutorials task (asked for by the user on 2026-09-12):

The user's words: "I would like a help > tutorials > * set of guides which walks you through basics of various features. Maybe a nice getting started tutorial, maybe a 'building components' walkthrough, etc. ... And maybe a first run experience which lets you get an intro to the app, or just gogogo. Use the design clickthroughs as inspiration, where you have pointers and can point to various parts of the application. Build a nice framework for defining these walkthroughs so that we can extend it over time. I'd like the tutorials system to be well organized and not just a long list of things."

The agreed shape (settled in the intake conversation, 2026-09-12):
- TRACKS, not a flat list. Help > Tutorials holds "Take the Tour" plus one SUBMENU per track, and a Tutorials window is the hub. The tracks are: Basics, Redlining, Looks, Colours & Styles, Building UI, Components, Video.
- A guide is DATA, not code: a Codable value in PhotonzCore describing steps. Adding a guide means adding data to the catalogue, and the menu, the window and the progress list all pick it up with no UI edited. That is the whole point of the framework and the thing that makes it extensible.
- Steps POINT AT REAL UI, clickthrough-style: a callout with a pointer aimed at a named control, not a page of prose.
- Design doc: docs/design/tutorials.md is the source of truth for the framework and the track list, written by the foundation task and extended by the rest.

THE TRAP that will waste a runner's day if it is not read first: the app already has a registry of named UI targets, the playtest harness (playtestControl / playtestField / steady names, Sources/Photonz/Playtest/PanelTarget.swift). It looks like exactly the right thing to reuse and it is NOT USABLE here: it is compiled out of the shipping build (Scripts/build-app.sh defines PHOTONZ_PLAYTEST for the dev and probe variants only, see docs/design/playtest-harness.md, "Who can run it"), and PanelTarget.swift:141 onwards is the no-op stub release actually gets. Tutorials ship to users, so the anchor registry has to be its own thing that is compiled IN for release. Model it on the playtest one - especially the STEADY NAME idea at PanelTarget.swift:126-138, a name taken off the model rather than off the copy, so rewording a label cannot break a guide - but do not depend on it.

Existing surfaces a tutorial entry point must fit with rather than duplicate:
- The Welcome window (Sources/Photonz/Welcome/WelcomeController.swift), first-run permissions setup, re-reachable from the menu-bar menu as "Welcome & Permissions...". It already owns first launch.
- The empty-editor onboarding card (Sources/Photonz/EditorView.swift:590-615): open a file, capture a rectangle, paste an image, blank canvas.
- There is NO Help menu in the app today: EditorCommands.swift declares Capture, Image, Video, Layer and the standard groups, and macOS supplies the default Help menu. Help > Tutorials has to be created.

Queue-driven app work targets the NEXT release unless the task says otherwise (CLAUDE.md), and a Current change is not finished until Next has it.
acceptance: Every guide in the track exists in the catalogue as data and appears under its track in the Help menu and the Tutorials window with no UI edited
Every guide runs start to finish in the real app, pointing at real controls, each one captured step by step in the audit
Every guide is short: a person can finish one in the time the entry claims, and the claim is measured rather than guessed
Every step points at something a person can actually see at that moment: nothing points at a control that is scrolled out of view, disabled or behind a closed panel without opening it first
A guide that needs something on the canvas brings its own sample document rather than depending on what the person has open
Copy obeys the repo rules: no em dashes, nothing about the tooling that built it, plain short human sentences
Every guide is checked with the features it teaches flagged off as well as on, and behaves sensibly either way
Audit under queue/audits/ with each guide captured step by step, and anything rough filed as a follow-up

log.note: Adversarial review before building (all measured on the probe, not read off the code): (1) the shelf remembers its scope and it starts on Media, so a step ringing the Library would have rung a shelf of screenshots; added a reveal-only prepare that turns it to Components, the same two lines Make Component already runs. (2) The starters include a component called Button, so the sample's is called Save Button or the shelf shows two identical tiles. (3) A document's picture is a layer called Background, so the sample's pieces are Box and Label. (4) A copy carries its original's name, so a page with two copies has three rows reading Save Button in the layers list: no step sends anybody in there. (5) A double click's FIRST click already selects, which raises the event a waiting step listens for, so no step both says double click and waits on a selection. (6) The button had to be 240 wide, not 176: at 176 the label filled the middle and a double click aimed at the box picked the text layer, the same trap the Looks track hit.

Three framework findings, each fixed where it happens rather than worked around in the guide: a rubber band round two layers never raised the layerSelected trigger (it lands in multiSelectedLayerIDs, not selectedLayerID), so a step saying "drag a box round both" watched somebody do it and did not move; the reveal stopped as soon as a SLIVER of a section was visible, so Make Component's own jump to the shelf left the Name box above the top of the panel with a ring round the two rows underneath it; and Add Version handed the keyboard to the new version's name field one pass too early, so typing went to the canvas.

Four guides land as data in TutorialGuides.swift with three samples (a button drawn as two loose layers, the same button already a component, and that original with two copies on it). Walked end to end on the probe, one walk each, all green: tutorial-make-a-component, tutorial-use-it-again-and-again, tutorial-override-one-copy, tutorial-component-versions. All 20 tutorial walks pass and Scripts/test.sh is green at 5909 tests. Checked in the real app with next-components off as well as on: the Components submenu and its four rows are gone from Help and from the Tutorials window with it off, and back with it on. Measured lengths against the claims: 114s/112s/111s under a 2 minute claim, 140s under a 3 minute one. Audit at queue/audits/2026-09-13-tutorials-components-track.json with five real window captures.

Two follow-ups filed, both p2 and both reproduced: a-copy-and-its-original-should-be-tellable-apart (three layers rows read Save Button once copies are placed, which is why no guide in the track uses the list), and find-out-why-the-effects-plus-goes-nameless-whil (one walk outside this track failed once under load looking for the Effects plus by name, and passed twice straight after). Sweep requested, because the reveal change can move the panel for up to a second longer than before.

Four guides under Help > Tutorials > Components, all data in TutorialGuides.swift: Make a component, Use it again and again, Override one copy, One name, two looks (planned as Variants, named for what the panel actually says). Three samples come with them. Walked end to end on the probe one walk per guide, all green, plus all 20 tutorial walks and Scripts/test.sh at 5909 tests. Checked in the app with next-components off as well as on. Three framework gaps fixed on the way: a rubber band selection now advances a waiting step, a step reveal holds out for the whole section rather than the first sliver, and a new reveal-only prepare turns the shelf to Components. Audit at queue/audits/2026-09-13-tutorials-components-track.json with five real window captures. Pushed as 823a9638.
